Marissa — high level notes and attachments attached for review. I focused on the architecture points they highlighted.

Summary (short):
- Dedicated: Dedicated GPU pools run in a Redwood-managed VPC. Customer workloads are isolated at the process and container level; network isolation is enforced with per-tenant subnetting + security groups. Only the inference control plane (authenticated API endpoints) is exposed to the public internet; backend traffic between control plane and GPUs is on private subnets. KV and prefix caches are stored in memory and ephemeral disk attached to the instance; persistence (if enabled) is encrypted at rest using customer-specific KMS keys for Dedicated customers.

- Private (VPC): Customer provides a VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink setup. We run the inference runtime in their VPC (customer-managed subnets) — network egress is controlled by their routing tables and NGFWs. Sensitive key material can be configured to use the customer's KMS/HSM. Audit logs (request traces, token-level metrics) can be forwarded to customer-owned CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Log Analytics via an IAM role.

Controls & notes:
- Tenant isolation: enforced via Kubernetes namespaces + strict RBAC + container-level seccomp profiles; no cross-tenant shared persistent volumes.
- KV cache: KV cache is in-process or in-memory Redis within the tenant boundary; multi-tenancy is avoided by dedicated Redis instances per tenant for Dedicated and full isolation for Private.
- Disk encryption: all disks encrypted (AES-256) at rest; key material managed via KMS; Dedicated supports per-customer KMS keys.
- Network egress: explicit egress rules; no default outbound to arbitrary endpoints.
- SOC 2 artefacts: we can provide redacted control narratives and the SOC 2 summary PDF (not the full report) — legal approval required for any full report sharing.

Attachments included for review:
- redwood-isolation-model-dedicated.pdf (draft)
- redwood-private-vpc-diagram.png (draft)
- SOC2-summary-redwood.pdf (summary only)

Comments / action items for Vivek: please flag anything that needs redaction or legal review. I kept the diagrams high-level (no internal hostnames).
